# Proverbs 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A crust of bread eaten in peace is better than a house full of feasting with constant fighting.

**2** A wise servant will end up in charge of a disgraceful son and will share the inheritance right alongside the other children.

**3** Silver is tested by the crucible and gold by the furnace, but the LORD is the one who tests human hearts.

**4** Bad people love listening to destructive talk, and liars are drawn to a poisonous tongue.

**5** Mocking someone because they're poor is an insult to the God who made them. Celebrating someone's misfortune will not go unpunished.

**6** Grandchildren are the pride and joy of the elderly, and children are proud of their parents.

**7** Eloquent words don't fit a fool — and lies are even more disgraceful coming from a leader.

**8** A bribe works like a charm for the person who gives it — it opens every door they approach.

**9** If you forgive an offense, you build love. If you keep bringing it up, you'll drive away your closest friend.

**10** One honest word of correction sinks deeper into a thoughtful person than a hundred punishments into a fool.

**11** Rebellious people are looking for nothing but trouble, and a ruthless response will be sent to deal with them.

**12** You'd be better off running into a mother bear whose cubs were stolen than crossing paths with a fool on a rampage.

**13** If you repay good with evil, trouble will never leave your house.

**14** Starting a fight is like opening a floodgate — once it starts, you can't stop it. Walk away before it escalates.

**15** Letting the guilty go free and punishing the innocent — the LORD finds both equally disgusting.

**16** What's the point of a fool having money to buy wisdom when they have no intention of learning?

**17** A real friend loves you no matter what, and a brother exists for moments of crisis.

**18** Only a person with no sense would co-sign a loan for a neighbor.

**19** People who love doing wrong love conflict. People who build their walls too high are inviting disaster.

**20** A person with a twisted heart never finds anything good, and a dishonest tongue gets its owner into trouble.

**21** Having a foolish child brings nothing but grief — there's no joy in being the parent of a fool.

**22** A cheerful heart is the best medicine, but a broken spirit drains you to the bone.

**23** A corrupt person takes bribes under the table to twist the course of justice.

**24** A wise person focuses on what matters, but a fool's attention wanders to the ends of the earth.

**25** A foolish child is a father's grief and a mother's bitter pain.

**26** It's wrong to penalize someone who's done the right thing, or to punish leaders for their integrity.

**27** A person who uses few words has real knowledge, and a calm disposition shows deep understanding.

**28** Even a fool looks smart when they keep their mouth shut. Closing your lips can make anyone seem wise.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **17:9**: Powerful relationship wisdom — if you forgive, love grows. If you keep rehashing old offenses, even your best friends will walk away.

- **17:17**: One of the most important verses on friendship in the Bible. Real friends don't disappear when things get hard — that's exactly when they show up.

- **17:22**: Ancient mind-body wisdom — your emotional state physically affects your health. Joy heals; despair deteriorates. Science has confirmed what Proverbs always knew.

— PNEUMA
